prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: one static Hearts of Iron IV stockpile-cost texticon, exact final canvas 30x12 pixels, shown inline beside a number.
Primary request: Create an original, nonfunctional miniature inventory glyph for a sealed biohazard-marked payload vial in a strategy-game stockpile.
Subject: One squat sealed capsule or laboratory-vial-shaped military supply object with a rounded body and short capped neck; add a distinct, simple three-lobed biohazard pictogram directly on a light band of the casing. The mark must remain bold at 30x12. This is symbolic icon art only; show no living organisms, pathogens, release, or technical construction detail.
Style/medium: Compact painted 2D inventory art with modest 1930s–1940s military materials, muted slate, olive-drab and aged brass, a small dark biohazard marking, restrained highlights, and crisp dark edge definition.
Composition/framing: One centered broad horizontal but visibly squat silhouette, about 2.2:1 width-to-height, designed to remain distinct beside numeric text at 30x12. Use a centered horizontal strip on the source canvas, a simple silhouette, inset complete edges, and transparent margin.
Lighting/mood: Even understated icon lighting with small metallic highlights only.
Constraints: Genuinely transparent unused canvas; no scene or floor; no text, letters, numbers, watermark, fumes, extra objects, tile, frame, border, badge, medallion, or separate emblem. The biohazard mark is painted directly on the object. Optimize both silhouette and mark for smooth downsampling to 30x12.
Avoid: Long rocket or missile profile, chemical-canister shape, living agents, release or attack scene, oversized badge, bright neon colors, chrome shine, modern equipment, cinematic lighting, fake checkerboard, opaque matte, colored halo, clipped edges, unintended transparent holes.
